title: External Validation of a Widely Implemented Proprietary Sepsis Prediction Model in Hospitalized Patients
supports_claim: External validation at Michigan Medicine (27,697 patients; 38,455 hospitalizations; Dec 2018-Oct 2019) found the Epic Sepsis Model had AUC 0.63 and only 33% sensitivity at the clinically used alert threshold, missing 67% of confirmed sepsis hospitalizations while alerting on 18% of all hospitalizations.
limitations: Single-site retrospective validation at one academic health system (Michigan Medicine); does not itself prove a specific patient was harmed, only that the alerting logic under-detects sepsis and over-alerts relative to the developer's reported performance; may not generalize to other hospitals, EHR configurations or later model versions/thresholds.

title: IBM's Watson supercomputer recommended 'unsafe and incorrect' cancer treatments, internal documents show
supports_claim: STAT News reported that internal IBM Watson Health slide presentations from 2017 documented 'multiple examples of unsafe and incorrect' cancer treatment recommendations from Watson for Oncology, and that the system was trained on synthetic/hypothetical cases curated by a small number of Memorial Sloan Kettering specialists rather than on real patient outcomes or broad clinical guidelines.
limitations: Based on leaked internal slide decks and named/anonymous sources reported by journalists, not a peer-reviewed study or regulatory audit; does not quantify how many real patients received unsafe recommendations in production use, nor document a specific confirmed patient injury.

title: AI chatbot maker Babylon Health attacks clinician in PR stunt after he goes public with safety concerns
supports_claim: TechCrunch reported that oncologist Dr. David Watkins, testing Babylon Health's symptom-checker chatbot over three years, documented cases where it failed to flag potential heart attack symptoms in female patients while suggesting panic attack or depression, and that Babylon's own rebuttal analysis counted 20 cases as 'genuine errors' among a disputed number of test triages.
limitations: Relies on one clinician's self-directed, non-randomized testing plus a company-authored rebuttal; the total test count and resulting error rate are actively disputed by both parties (Babylon: ~2,400 tests; Watkins: ~800-900 complete triages), so no single audited error rate is settled fact; not a controlled trial or independent regulator audit.

title: Annex III: High-Risk AI Systems Referred to in Article 6(2)
publisher: European Commission - AI Act Service Desk
supports_claim: Official EU page states Annex III point 5(d) classifies as high-risk 'AI systems intended to evaluate and classify emergency calls... as well as of emergency healthcare patient triage systems', and point 5(a) covers AI used to evaluate eligibility for essential public services including healthcare.
limitations: Page is a living regulatory reference without a single publish date; whether TriageAssist (a non-emergency telehealth callback triage tool, not an emergency dispatch/911-equivalent system) falls inside or outside the Annex III 5(d) wording is not self-evident from the text alone and needs qualified legal interpretation.

title: Vietnam AI Law 134/2025/QH15
supports_claim: Vietnam's AI Law took effect on 2026-03-01 and establishes the general legal scope and obligations for AI systems in Vietnam, including risk-tiering concepts.
limitations: The law text sets the general framework; it does not by itself enumerate whether a telehealth triage assistant is classified as high-risk. Exact obligations depend on how the use case maps to the implementing decrees and the official high-risk list.

title: Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg high-risk AI list
supports_claim: This decision publishes Vietnam's official list of high-risk AI systems and took effect on 2026-08-15.
limitations: The specific TriageAssist use case (telehealth symptom triage assistant) has not yet been checked against the full published list item by item; title-level review alone is insufficient to confirm inclusion or exclusion.
